arguments.value: Severe posterior fossa mass presenting with headache, neck pain, gait instability, vertigo, and right-sided weakness, with MRI showing a large right cerebellar lesion causing mass effect, obstructive hydrocephalus, and tonsillar wedging. She underwent right suboccipital craniectomy with total resection; histology confirmed small-cell glioblastoma. Postoperatively, she completed radiotherapy with concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide and remained neurologically well with no recurrence on follow-up for more than two years.
